Scenarios

Create test items

Create a small, isolated item family that proves two supply patterns — purchased components and a Job Shop finished product — and carry it through the engineering, costing, and stock data a quantity-one production order needs, so the finished item can be produced and received into the finished-goods warehouse.

  1. 1Confirm the test design10 steps
  2. 2Create two item groups6 steps
  3. 3Configure the purchased group14 steps
  4. 4Configure the made group10 steps
  5. 5Verify site creation control4 steps
  6. 6Create the three items11 steps
  7. 7Build the job shop bill of material19 steps
  8. 8Build the job shop routing19 steps
  9. 9Confirm costing data6 steps
  10. 10Stock the components10 steps
  11. 11Qualify the training case7 steps
Start

Different cases

  • Minimum two-item test

    Create only one purchased material and one Job Shop finished product. This proves the two supply patterns but gives the later BOM only one material class

  • Recommended three-item test

    Use this full walkthrough: two purchased inputs and one Job Shop finished product

  • Four-item multilevel test

    Add a semi-finished level only after the single-level case works; it requires another made-item master, BOM, routing, and costing layer, and a second production order

  • Purchased finished goods

    Use another dedicated Product group with Default Supply Source = Purchase; no Job Shop Production defaults are required, and phases 6–7 do not apply

  • Production quantity greater than one

    Book proportionally more component stock in task 10 — 2 rods and 1 sleeve per pair. Nothing in the phase structure changes

  • Items only

    Stop after task 6. The family exists as master data but cannot be produced; phases 6–10 are what make it runnable

Warehousing➔Master Data➔Warehouses➔Warehouses

Why this task Something went wrong Read it to me

Nothing yet. Every later phase reads a value recorded here, and the one that bites is the warehouse type: a Shop Floor warehouse cannot be received into as a Normal one can, and a description does not say which it is. In this environment purchase against manufacture is a supply-source decision rather than an item-type one, because physical items are all type Product.

  • An example item code already exists

    Choose another unused code; do not reuse or repurpose an existing item

  • A candidate “raw material” warehouse is Shop Floor

    Select an approved Normal warehouse; do not rely on description alone

Why this task Something went wrong Read it to me

Item Defaults is keyed by item type and item group, so the group is the handle every default hangs on. Two groups exist because the two roles need different supply sources, and a group is nothing more than a code, a description and a currency until task 3 attaches defaults to it.

Master Data➔Items➔Defaults➔Item Defaults

Why this task Something went wrong Read it to me

A default combination records, per package, two separate things: whether default data exists for the subentity, shown by the indicator, and whether a new item should receive it, set by the Create check box. A green indicator with the box cleared gives a new item nothing. The Sites check box decides whether new items get a site row automatically.

  • Product is unavailable

    Confirm the environment's Product-active setting; do not substitute Purchased or Manufactured without approval

  • Ordering defaults appear to require a Warehouse, but no Warehouse field is displayed

    Verify the warehouse on the parent tcibd0502m000 Sites row

  • Ordering defaults will not save

    Confirm every visible required value and retain the proposed Economic Order Quantity

  • Purchase defaults will not save

    Confirm the units, currency, price group and statistics group in the family sheet §4

  • Warehousing defaults show an unknown required policy value

    Stop and obtain the approved value; do not invent valuation, ownership, location, lot/serial, or handling-unit policy

Master Data➔Items➔Defaults➔Item Defaults

Why this task Read it to me

> Warning > The Production and Sales portions of this phase were walked in Company 4100 on 2026-08-16. The values in the family sheet combine an approved Product/Job Shop reference, the existing M010 finished-goods defaults, and the Company 4100 reference currency. Do not reuse them in another company without repeating those checks.

The same mechanism as task 3 with a different supply source and two more packages. Job Shop names manufacture at a production facility as the default source and creates nothing else, and the Production defaults session only opens when Job Shop by Site is active. A Sales default change offers to propagate to existing items, which for an isolated new group is declined.

Master Data➔Items➔Defaults➔Item Control and Defaults by Site

Why this task Something went wrong Read it to me

> Warning > This phase has not been walked for the new groups. Capture the Centrally Managed state and the saved Create controls.

The Create controls can be governed at the site instead of the company. When Centrally Managed is selected the site mirrors the company defaults and the controls are disabled here; when it is cleared the site's own controls decide, and an item created before this is checked can arrive with fewer subentities than its group promised, with no message naming the cause.

  • Site Create controls are disabled

    Read Centrally Managed; when selected, correct the governing tcibd0502m000 control instead of the site row

Master Data➔Items➔Items

Why this task Something went wrong Read it to me

> Note > All three items were created this way in Company 4100 on 2026-08-16 and their CSADNA01 site rows verified. Create the two purchased items first and the pair last, and do not create the pair until task 4 has approved Production and Sales defaults. Not documented for this release.

> Note > The Item identifier has separate Project and Item portions. These are standard test items: leave Project blank and enter the BAM-* code in the Item portion. If General Projects tcmcs0152s000 opens from the Project lookup, close it without creating a project.

On save, LN gives the new item the supply source, units and subentities its group's defaults promised and, if the Sites box was set, a site row. The saved site row is where the promise is checked: the supply source and the indicators on it prove phases 2 to 4, which is why nothing inheritable is typed here.

  • The item code is rejected

    Follow the current item-code segmentation; do not modify segmentation for the experiment

  • The save is refused for a field this walkthrough does not name

    Record the field label and the message. Do not clear another value to force the save — the 2026-08-16 run found Grade this way

  • A subentity is missing after save

    Recheck task 3 for a purchased item, task 4 for the pair, and task 5 for both

  • Actual supply differs from the default

    Check for item-level overrides and date-effective supply source before changing the default

Manufacturing➔Job Shop➔Engineering➔Bills of Material

Why this task Something went wrong Read it to me

> Prerequisite > Task 6 complete: all three items exist and each site row shows its intended Default Supply Source. Job Shop by Site must be Active or In Preparation in Concept Activation tcemm4600m000 — the same setting task 4's Production defaults depend on. It is confirmed Active here: the 2026-09-02 Job Shop Master Data Parameters form displays a field its help shows only under Active.

A bill of material is written against the item, per site, and cannot be used for manufacture until its revision is approved; approval and the two use indicators, for planning and for costing, are three separate actions. The material lines carry the issuing warehouse, and the revision's effective date decides whether a production order's reference date selects it.

  • The BOM header will not save

    Confirm Site, Product, BOM Quantity, and Effective Date. Do not clear a proposed required value to make the save pass

  • The BOM stays at New

    Only Approved bills of material can be used for manufacture. Run Actions➔Approve Revision on the selected row

  • Use for Planning is refused

    Another BOM already holds it for this item and site — one per item and site for planning, one per product for costing

Manufacturing➔Job Shop➔Engineering➔Job Shop Routings

Why this task Something went wrong Read it to me

> Prerequisite > An existing work center and an existing reference operation for the site. This walkthrough does not create work centers, machines, or reference operations. Look them up first — Manufacturing ➔ Job Shop ➔ Shop Layout ➔ Work Centers tirou0101m000 and Manufacturing ➔ Job Shop ➔ Shop Layout ➔ Reference Operations tirou4150m000 — and if neither has a usable entry for the site, stop and obtain one.

The routing gives the production order operations to report complete; without one there are no estimated production costs and nothing triggers the finished-goods receipt. A reference operation is a template that carries its own times into the operation line, and the routing quantity is what makes those times the times for one pair.

  • Work Center or Reference Operation is rejected

    Use an existing approved value. Do not create a work center, task, or machine from this walkthrough

  • The operation line will not save

    Every column the screen marks required must be filled — Operation, Reference Operation, and Work Center at minimum

Common➔Standard Costs➔Master Data➔Item - Costing

Why this task Something went wrong Read it to me

A production order's estimate reads each material's standard cost, and a parameter decides whether a missing one stops the calculation or silently lowers it. Purchased items get their standard cost from purchase price data, so the two components will have none until task 10 buys them in.

  • A purchased component has no standard cost

    Its standard cost is calculated from purchase price priority levels; the item needs purchase price data before it will have one

Warehousing➔Inventory 360

Why this task Something went wrong Read it to me

A production order can be created and released with no stock, but it cannot be finished, because the material issue has nothing to issue. Buying the components in exercises the Purchase defaults and creates the purchase price history their standard cost is calculated from; the inventory figure at the raw-material warehouse, not the receipt status, is the proof.

  • On-hand does not increase after booking

    Do not book again. Find the order or transaction that was created and check its status first — a second booking doubles the error

Scenarios

Run order planning

Make one finished item visible to planning, give it a demand it cannot cover from stock, run MRP, and read the result — a planned supply chain covering the shortfall — in the Item Order Plan, in Planned Orders, and in the pegging tree.

  1. 1Make the item visible to planning6 steps
  2. 2Create demand3 steps
  3. 3Put the demand inside the horizon4 steps
  4. 4Run MRP4 steps
  5. 5Review the result5 steps
  6. 6Read the pegging tree4 steps
Start

Different cases

  • Run planning for all items

    Generate Order Planning cprrp1210m000, Planning➔Order Planning➔Generate Order Planning, runs ranges instead of one item — the production habit. No help is filed for it, so its options are not assumed to match cprrp1220m000's

  • Net change instead of regenerative

    Run a Net Change Planning in the generate session — simulates only from the first net-change date. A value change inside one step, not a phase change

  • Master planning

    A different mechanism, not a value change: enabling Master Plan on cprpd1100m000 splits the horizons, and the item master plan must be initialized before it exists. Own walkthrough when written — it needs cprpd/cprmp session help first

> Prerequisite > A finished item with an Approved BOM and routing, components, and stock data — the qualified training case from Create test items. The 2026-08-20 session used BAM-CHOP-PAIR with components BAM-ROD and BAM-SLEEVE.

The planning screens read an item's planning data, and an item that has none is not refused; it is absent, with nothing to explain why. The link is a row for the planning cluster on the item, and MRP plans a BOM component only if the component has planning data of its own, so this phase checks every item in the structure, not just the parent.

Sales➔Orders➔Order Intake Workbench

Why this task Something went wrong A different case Read it to me

Planning acts on uncovered demand. A sales order for more than is on hand creates a shortfall, and that shortfall is exactly the quantity MRP should propose, which is what makes the run checkable. Planning sees the demand without the order being approved.

  • LN refuses the item on the sales order — "item sales by sales office not present"

    The item has no row for the order's sales office. Add it on the Sales Offices tab of Item tcibd0501m100, then close and reopen the order session

  • A master-data fix appears to have no effect

    The session was already open when the data changed. Close it and reopen — observed twice on 2026-08-20

  • Change or cancel an order line

    Change or cancel a sales order line after it is entered.

    1. change or cancel the line on the sales order; once it is released, the warehouse decides whether that is still allowed
    2. if the change is allowed, the outbound line follows it, and its advice and picking list are deleted
    3. if cancelling is no longer allowed, finish the shipment with a shipped quantity of 0 and return the goods to stock with a transfer order
    4. Not documented for this release.
  • Rush an order

    Give a sales order, or one line of it, the highest priority through the warehouse.

    1. choose Rush Order on the sales order, or Rush Order Line on one line; the order's priority becomes 1
    2. release it to warehousing, where its outbound lines are advised and processed before any others
    3. Not documented for this release.

Why this task Something went wrong Read it to me

The order horizon decides which demand planning sees at all: demand beyond it is not late or flagged, it does not exist to planning. LN turns the number of days you enter into a date by counting workdays on the calendar of the item's warehouse, so the date it shows is the one to trust.

Why this task Something went wrong Read it to me

The run reads every demand inside the horizon, nets it against stock and existing supply, and generates planned orders for the shortfall, multi-level through the BOM when child items are included. With pegging relations updated it also records which demand each planned order exists to serve, which is what task 6 reads.

  • The run plans the parent but not a component

    The component has no planning data of its own. Step task 1, step 6 — MRP skips it silently

  • The run produces nothing at all, or nothing propagates to the parent

    Check which item you launched the generation on. Running it from a component does not traverse upward — re-run from the top-level (finished) item, per step task 4, step 1

  • A component was given planning data and still does not appear

    It may be correctly absent — planning proposes supply only for what stock does not cover. Read the component's own Item Order Plan and its on-hand before assuming the fix failed. Observed unexplained on 2026-08-25

Why this task Something went wrong Read it to me

One planned order plays two roles: it is supply on the parent's plan and demand on the component's, and the component's own plan has already answered it. Planned quantities equal the raw shortfall only when the item's ordering data imposes no lot-size rule; a minimum or a multiple changes the number before you see it.

  • A planned quantity does not equal the raw shortfall

    Order-quantity rules in Items - Ordering tcibd2100m000 round it — "Lot sizing", cpordplanug p. 21

  • An expected planned purchase order is missing entirely

    If the item is a purchase schedule item, supply transfers straight to Purchase Control and no planned purchase order is created — cprrp1100m000 help

The pegging tree walks the relations the run recorded: upstream, what will supply this demand; downstream, what demand caused this order. The tree exists only if pegging relations were generated, which in this environment happens on every run because the option is locked on.

Needs: Know the item's stock before you start: Check an item's inventory.

Start

Different cases

  • Purchase with inspection

    An inspection activity sits between receipt and put-away. Warehouse Inspections whinh3122m000 runs against a receipt in this environment. This adds a phase and would earn its own walkthrough.

  • Direct-delivery purchase

    Goods ship from the supplier to a customer without entering your warehouse. That removes phases 3–5 entirely, so it is a different process, not a variant of this one

  • Booking opening stock instead of buying

    The adjustment route the notes of Create test items phase 9 describe — a cycle counting/adjustment order. Faster, but it bypasses purchase defaults and leaves no purchase price history. Its entry session was never captured

Nothing yet. A confirmed receipt is a document reaching a status; only the on-hand figure at the receiving warehouse proves stock moved, and it cannot prove anything unless it was read before the order existed. A new item is not necessarily at zero.

Start

Different cases

  • More than one component

    Record and compare every expected component and estimated quantity in task 3; issue every material line in task 5; the phase structure does not change

  • Revision-controlled item

    The qualified training case must include the item revision as well as BOM and routing revisions

  • No routing

    Outside this basic foundation. The help states that no estimated production costs are defined when the order has no routing

Why this task Something went wrong A different case Read it to me

Material issue turns the estimated quantities into an outbound warehousing order from the raw-material warehouse to the work center, and each issued quantity books a WIP transaction. That first WIP transaction is what moves the order to Active; release alone does not. How much of the outbound procedure LN runs for you depends on two check boxes on the material line.

  • The material line stays blocked / To Issue by Warehouse never appears

    Run Initiate Inventory Issue tisfc0207m000 manually; if still blocked, stop and record what was observed

  • Generate/Release Outbound Advice are missing or already actioned

    Do not assume a fault. Direct Process Warehouse Order Line may be automatic for this material — confirm in Activities by Warehousing Order whinh2104m000 before troubleshooting further

Manufacturing➔Job Shop➔Production Control➔Report Operations

Why this task Something went wrong A different case Read it to me

Reporting the last operation complete records the quantity produced and, depending on a parameter, posts it to inventory silently, not at all, or after asking. The order becomes Production Completed when reported and Completed only when Warehousing finishes the inbound receipt, so the two statuses are a handoff, not a failure. The phase ends with an inventory read because the Manufacturing-side status alone does not prove the stock arrived.

  • Report Orders Completed does not open after the last operation

    Stop and record the operation's status and any message; this dialog's trigger condition is not documented

  • Quantity Delivered stays at 0 or finished-item on-hand does not increase

    The production receipt warehousing order may need manual processing, like task 5's issue order. Check Warehousing Orders whinh2100m000 for an open receipt order before assuming an error

  • Components short at release

    Decide whether a production order releases while a component is short. Not documented for this release.

    Set in: Release Production Orders

  • Manual production order

    Make an item on a production order entered by hand.

    1. create the production order
    2. release it
  • Report Operations

    Issue the material and report the work done.

    1. issue the material
    2. report the operations and the order completed
  • More than one operation

    Confirm every expected operation in routing sequence in task 3; report each one complete in task 6 (step task 6, step 4); the phase structure does not change

Different cases

  • Multicompany warehouse transfer — source and destination warehouses in different logistic companies

    LN generates two warehousing orders instead of one: the ship-from company's order carries the outbound and shipment activities, the ship-to company's carries inbound and inspection. Ship-to Code becomes meaningful. This changes the phase structure (an order-handoff phase is needed) and earns its own walkthrough rather than a bullet here

  • Planned/automated transfer, driven by Order Planning

    Transfer Order Planning cppat1210m000, reached via Planning➔Plan Transfer➔Transfer Order Planning, generates transfer orders from planned inventory transactions rather than a person entering one by hand. Out of scope for this walkthrough.

  • Serialized or lot-controlled item

    The order header's Reclassification tab applies to rental and serialized transfers specifically. This variant is outside the scope of the base walkthrough. Source: Infor LN help for Warehousing Order whinh2100m100, Field Information — Reclassification (Rental Product Transfer, Serial Number)

Why this task Something went wrong Read it to me

Nothing new. A transfer is proved twice: the source down and the destination up by the same quantity. The one run on file satisfied only the second half, which is why this phase reads both.

Source on-hand before minus source on-hand after must equal the transferred quantity, and destination on-hand after minus destination on-hand before must equal the same figure. The walkthrough is complete only when both hold.

Sales➔Orders➔Order Intake Workbench

Why this task Something went wrong A different case Read it to me

Approving the order is what makes its lines eligible for warehousing: LN releases only approved lines, and an unapproved order fails at the next phase with no obvious reason. The Order Acknowledgement that prints carries the sales order number, which the warehousing order will inherit.

  • Status stuck on Free

    Not approved — Actions➔Approve

  • On-hand looks sufficient but the order will not fill

    Check Allocated — much of the on-hand may be committed elsewhere. See task 1, step 4

  • Stock promised to other orders

    Decide silently how much of on-hand is free for this order, which is the available-to-promise check. The figure decision 2 really tests is projected inventory, time-phased, not the on-hand total — Item Order Plan §task 3, step 1. Not documented for this release.

    Read it on: Item Order Plan

    Set in: Items - Planning

  • Change or cancel an order line

    Change or cancel a sales order line after it is entered.

    1. change or cancel the line on the sales order; once it is released, the warehouse decides whether that is still allowed
    2. if the change is allowed, the outbound line follows it, and its advice and picking list are deleted
    3. if cancelling is no longer allowed, finish the shipment with a shipped quantity of 0 and return the goods to stock with a transfer order
    4. Not documented for this release.
  • Rush an order

    Give a sales order, or one line of it, the highest priority through the warehouse.

    1. choose Rush Order on the sales order, or Rush Order Line on one line; the order's priority becomes 1
    2. release it to warehousing, where its outbound lines are advised and processed before any others
    3. Not documented for this release.
  • Direct delivery

    Have the supplier deliver straight to the customer, so that Warehousing is not involved.

    1. set the line's delivery type to Direct Delivery, by hand or from the shortage menu that appears when stock is short
    2. generate the purchase order for the line, from a purchase order advice or directly
    3. record the supplier's receipt in Procurement and send the delivery back to the sales order
    4. Not documented for this release.
  • Cross-docking

    Fill a sales order that has no stock by taking inbound goods straight from receipt to the staging location.

    1. set the line's delivery type to Cross-docking, by hand or from the shortage menu that appears when stock is short
    2. generate the purchase order for the line, from a purchase order advice or directly
    3. release the purchase order and the sales order to warehousing
    4. Not documented for this release.

Sales➔Orders➔Order Intake Workbench

Why this task Something went wrong A different case Read it to me

A sales order for more pairs than exist creates the shortfall the rest of the chain answers. Planning will see it only if its delivery date falls inside the item's order horizon, which LN computes in workdays on a calendar, and the order is approved now because task 7's release needs it, not because planning does.

  • LN refuses the item on the sales order

    No row for the order's sales office on the Sales Offices tab of Item tcibd0501m100. Add it, then close and reopen the order session

  • The demand does not appear in the Item Order Plan

    The delivery date is beyond the Order Horizon date. Step task 2, step 5 — and the date is not today plus your days

  • Stock promised to other orders

    Decide silently how much of on-hand is free for this order, which is the available-to-promise check. The figure decision 2 really tests is projected inventory, time-phased, not the on-hand total — Item Order Plan §task 3, step 1. Not documented for this release.

    Read it on: Item Order Plan

    Set in: Items - Planning

    Decide silently whether planning can see the item and every component beneath it.

    Read it on: Items - Planning

    Set in: Item

  • Inside the order horizon

    Decide silently whether the delivery date is near enough to plan. Counted in workdays.

    Read it on: Item Order Plan

    Set in: Items - Planning

  • Change or cancel an order line

    Change or cancel a sales order line after it is entered.

    1. change or cancel the line on the sales order; once it is released, the warehouse decides whether that is still allowed
    2. if the change is allowed, the outbound line follows it, and its advice and picking list are deleted
    3. if cancelling is no longer allowed, finish the shipment with a shipped quantity of 0 and return the goods to stock with a transfer order
    4. Not documented for this release.
  • Rush an order

    Give a sales order, or one line of it, the highest priority through the warehouse.

    1. choose Rush Order on the sales order, or Rush Order Line on one line; the order's priority becomes 1
    2. release it to warehousing, where its outbound lines are advised and processed before any others
    3. Not documented for this release.
  • Direct delivery

    Have the supplier deliver straight to the customer, so that Warehousing is not involved.

    1. set the line's delivery type to Direct Delivery, by hand or from the shortage menu that appears when stock is short
    2. generate the purchase order for the line, from a purchase order advice or directly
    3. record the supplier's receipt in Procurement and send the delivery back to the sales order
    4. Not documented for this release.
  • Cross-docking

    Fill a sales order that has no stock by taking inbound goods straight from receipt to the staging location.

    1. set the line's delivery type to Cross-docking, by hand or from the shortage menu that appears when stock is short
    2. generate the purchase order for the line, from a purchase order advice or directly
    3. release the purchase order and the sales order to warehousing
    4. Not documented for this release.

Why this task Something went wrong Read it to me

MRP nets the demand against stock and generates a planned production order for the pairs, then, through the BOM, planned purchase orders for the rods the pairs need. The arithmetic in the pegging tree is the test that it did so correctly.

  • The run plans the pair but not a component

    The component has no planning data of its own. Step task 1, step 4 — MRP skips it silently

  • A component has plan data and still produces nothing

    It may be correctly absent — planning proposes supply only for what stock does not cover. Read its own Item Order Plan and on-hand

  • The pegging tree is empty

    Pegging relations were not generated, or the demand is beyond the Pegging Horizon in Planning Parameters cprpd0100m000

Planning➔Order Planning➔Confirm Order Planning

Why this task Something went wrong A different case Read it to me

> Warning > The purchase half of this phase is walked; the production half has never been run here. On 2026-08-25 two planned purchase orders for BAM-ROD became purchase order 100000682. The two planned production orders beside them were deliberately left untransferred and remain at Planned. Step task 4, step 6 is therefore the one step in this walkthrough nobody has performed — you are testing it, not using it.

A planned order is a proposal that no other module can see. Confirming marks it approved, and transferring translates it: a planned production order becomes a production order in Job Shop Control and a planned purchase order becomes a purchase order in Procurement, decided by the item's supply source. A transfer run against unconfirmed orders appears to do nothing.

  • The transfer runs and nothing happens

    The orders were still Planned. Step task 4, step 3. There is no message for "nothing matched"

  • "Buy-from BP cannot be determined for item …"

    No partner row on the item's Item - Business Partner tab. Steps task 4, step 1–task 4, step 2. The failed proposal survives, so fix it and rerun

  • Purchase Order Type is blank

    LN gives an error. This environment defaults IPO

  • Confirm Order Planning

    Confirm planned orders before they are transferred.

    1. confirm the planned orders, then transfer them
  • Build by hand instead of from planning

    Skip step task 4, step 6 and create the production order directly per Production order task 2. This is the only production path anyone here has walked — it is the fallback if step task 4, step 6 fails

Why this task Something went wrong A different case Read it to me

The sales order from task 2 is released to warehousing, advised, picked, frozen and confirmed, exactly as in the ship-from-stock walkthrough. On-hand at the shipping warehouse down by the shipped quantity is the completion test for the whole chain.

  • Advice greyed out

    You are on the session toolbar. The advice actions live on the Outbound Lines toolbar — step task 7, step 3

  • The order will not advise

    The header Warehouse does not hold the stock. Recheck against task 1, step 2

  • The shipment will not confirm

    The line was never picked, or the shipment was never frozen. Steps task 7, step 4 and task 7, step 5

    Decide whether outbound advice is generated when stock is short. Not documented for this release.

    Set in: Inventory Handling Parameters

  • Shipped less than picked

    Ship less than was picked; the rest becomes Not Shipped Quantity on the shipment line, and a backorder follows once the shipment is confirmed. Not documented for this release.

    Read it on: Shipment Lines

    Set in: Sales Order Parameters

  • Blocked release

    Stop a sales order line from releasing.

    1. read why it is blocked: an order over the credit limit, overdue invoices, a margin exceeded, a failed export or letter-of-credit check, or a reason someone set by hand
    2. release it in Blocked Sales Order (Lines) tdsls4520m000, a session in neither menu extract
    3. a user can release only the kinds of hold their profile allows, set in User Profiles tdsls0139m000, Sales➔Master Data➔General➔User Profiles
    4. Not documented for this release.

Search

  • ProblemAn example item code already exists

    Choose another unused code; do not reuse or repurpose an existing item

  • ProblemA candidate “raw material” warehouse is Shop Floor

    Select an approved Normal warehouse; do not rely on description alone

  • ProblemEither item-group code already exists

    Use new dedicated group codes rather than changing an existing group

  • ProblemProduct is unavailable

    Confirm the environment's Product-active setting; do not substitute Purchased or Manufactured without approval

  • ProblemOrdering defaults appear to require a Warehouse, but no Warehouse field is displayed

    Verify the warehouse on the parent tcibd0502m000 Sites row

  • ProblemOrdering defaults will not save

    Confirm every visible required value and retain the proposed Economic Order Quantity

  • ProblemPurchase defaults will not save

    Confirm the units, currency, price group and statistics group in the family sheet §4

  • ProblemWarehousing defaults show an unknown required policy value

    Stop and obtain the approved value; do not invent valuation, ownership, location, lot/serial, or handling-unit policy

  • ProblemSite Create controls are disabled

    Read Centrally Managed; when selected, correct the governing tcibd0502m000 control instead of the site row

  • ProblemThe item code is rejected

    Follow the current item-code segmentation; do not modify segmentation for the experiment

  • ProblemThe save is refused for a field this walkthrough does not name

    Record the field label and the message. Do not clear another value to force the save — the 2026-08-16 run found Grade this way

  • ProblemA subentity is missing after save

    Recheck task 3 for a purchased item, task 4 for the pair, and task 5 for both

  • ProblemActual supply differs from the default

    Check for item-level overrides and date-effective supply source before changing the default

  • ProblemThe BOM header will not save

    Confirm Site, Product, BOM Quantity, and Effective Date. Do not clear a proposed required value to make the save pass

  • ProblemThe BOM stays at New

    Only Approved bills of material can be used for manufacture. Run Actions➔Approve Revision on the selected row

  • ProblemUse for Planning is refused

    Another BOM already holds it for this item and site — one per item and site for planning, one per product for costing

  • ProblemWork Center or Reference Operation is rejected

    Use an existing approved value. Do not create a work center, task, or machine from this walkthrough

  • ProblemThe operation line will not save

    Every column the screen marks required must be filled — Operation, Reference Operation, and Work Center at minimum

  • ProblemA purchased component has no standard cost

    Its standard cost is calculated from purchase price priority levels; the item needs purchase price data before it will have one

  • ProblemOn-hand does not increase after booking

    Do not book again. Find the order or transaction that was created and check its status first — a second booking doubles the error

  • ProblemThe production order opens with no BOM or routing

    Compare the order's reference date with the effective dates from steps task 7, step 7 and task 8, step 7. A revision effective after the reference date is not selected

  • ProblemThe production order has no operation to report complete

    Recheck task 8 — an approved routing with at least one operation is what task 6 of the production-order walkthrough reports against

  • ProblemThe item is not in the Item Order Plan

    It has no planning data — no cluster row, no plan. Steps task 1, step 3–task 1, step 5. Not an error state; nothing will tell you

  • ProblemLN refuses the item on the sales order — "item sales by sales office not present"

    The item has no row for the order's sales office. Add it on the Sales Offices tab of Item tcibd0501m100, then close and reopen the order session

  • ProblemA master-data fix appears to have no effect

    The session was already open when the data changed. Close it and reopen — observed twice on 2026-08-20

  • ProblemThe demand does not appear in the Item Order Plan

    The delivery date is beyond the Order Horizon date. Step task 3, step 2 — and remember the date is not today plus your days

  • ProblemThe run plans the parent but not a component

    The component has no planning data of its own. Step task 1, step 6 — MRP skips it silently

  • ProblemThe run produces nothing at all, or nothing propagates to the parent

    Check which item you launched the generation on. Running it from a component does not traverse upward — re-run from the top-level (finished) item, per step task 4, step 1

  • ProblemA component was given planning data and still does not appear

    It may be correctly absent — planning proposes supply only for what stock does not cover. Read the component's own Item Order Plan and its on-hand before assuming the fix failed. Observed unexplained on 2026-08-25

  • ProblemA planned quantity does not equal the raw shortfall

    Order-quantity rules in Items - Ordering tcibd2100m000 round it — "Lot sizing", cpordplanug p. 21

  • ProblemAn expected planned purchase order is missing entirely

    If the item is a purchase schedule item, supply transfers straight to Purchase Control and no planned purchase order is created — cprrp1100m000 help

  • ProblemThe pegging tree is empty

    Pegging relations were not generated, or the demand lies beyond the Pegging Horizon cprpd0100m000. See the task 6 Prerequisite

  • ProblemThe item returns no row

    The item has no inventory records yet, so there is nothing to report

  • ProblemItem Order Plan is greyed out in the header

    Expected. Open it through Planning, as the task 1 notes say

  • ProblemOn hand looks sufficient but an order will not fill

    Check Inventory Allocated. Much of the on-hand may be committed elsewhere

  • ProblemEconomic Stock is negative

    The warehouse is over-allocated: more is committed than it holds and expects

  • ProblemOrder type is not IPO

    Nothing. IPO is what this environment defaulted on one dated run, not a required value

  • ProblemNo warehousing order appears after saving the purchase order

    The warehouse on the order lines (task 3, step 4). Without one, there is nothing for LN to raise an inbound order against. Then the purchase order's Release to Warehousing tab: a line still sitting there has not been released, and Purchase Order Line Status tdpur4534m000 names the activity it is waiting on

  • ProblemThe Actions menu offers no receive command

    The order origin. An outbound order carries outbound activities; confirm you opened the generated inbound order from task 4, step 1, not the purchase order

  • Problemwhinh0032 at the receipt

    The message names missing stock point details for the receipt line. Capture the LOG detail before clearing it — and afterwards, read the receipt's Errors Logged flag and Receipt Message Log whinh3530m000, which hold the messages once the dialog is gone

  • ProblemThe receipt looks confirmed but nothing was received

    Whether the receipt has any lines at all. whinh3512m000's help states Confirmed is cleared when the receipt has no receipt lines — the same cleared box as a receipt whose lines are merely unconfirmed

  • ProblemThe receipt confirms but on-hand does not move

    Whether All Lines Final and All Lines Complete were both set (task 5, step 4), and whether the receiving warehouse in task 6 is the one from task 1, step 1

  • ProblemNo qualified item/BOM/routing combination is available

    Stop. This walkthrough does not create or repair master data; request a qualified training case

  • ProblemComponent has no suitable warehouse stock

    Choose another qualified case or replenish it before creating an order intended for later execution

  • ProblemThe item or revision is rejected

    Stop and have the master-data owner verify the existing item and revision; do not change setup from this walkthrough

  • ProblemThe order does not save at Created

    Record the message and visible fields; do not substitute guessed values

  • ProblemBOM or routing is blank or unexpected

    Check the qualified dates/revisions and record the mismatch

  • ProblemValidation reports a multilevel BOM loop

    Stop. Do not improvise a replacement component or revision; the supported correction route is not yet documented

  • ProblemExpected operation or component is absent

    Leave the order at Created and return it to the master-data owner for diagnosis

  • ProblemThe order does not reach Released

    Record the message; the release options this walkthrough does not exercise (shortages, quality, printing) may be blocking it — check them against Production Order Parameters tisfc0100s000 before assuming a fault

  • ProblemThe material line stays blocked / To Issue by Warehouse never appears

    Run Initiate Inventory Issue tisfc0207m000 manually; if still blocked, stop and record what was observed

  • ProblemGenerate/Release Outbound Advice are missing or already actioned

    Do not assume a fault. Direct Process Warehouse Order Line may be automatic for this material — confirm in Activities by Warehousing Order whinh2104m000 before troubleshooting further

  • ProblemReport Orders Completed does not open after the last operation

    Stop and record the operation's status and any message; this dialog's trigger condition is not documented

  • ProblemQuantity Delivered stays at 0 or finished-item on-hand does not increase

    The production receipt warehousing order may need manual processing, like task 5's issue order. Check Warehousing Orders whinh2100m000 for an open receipt order before assuming an error

  • ProblemNo order number appears

    Header not saved, or a required field is still blank — recheck task 2, step 3–task 2, step 6

  • ProblemAdvice greyed out

    You are on the session toolbar, not the Outbound Lines toolbar — see task 3, step 6

  • ProblemNo Run appears on the Picking List

    If the order already advanced, record Automatic / not observed. Otherwise, picking may not apply or advice was not generated; return to task 3

  • ProblemNo shipment is visible for a different-warehouse transfer

    Official help says Create Shipment is Always. Check Shipment Lines and the task 3 activity status before continuing

  • ProblemConfirm greyed out

    Shipment not yet Frozen, or Freeze Mandatory requires it — run task 5, step 3 first

  • ProblemDestination on-hand did not rise

    The receipt in task 6 was not confirmed — return to the inbound line and Warehouse Receipt

  • ProblemSource and destination changes do not both equal the transfer quantity

    Do not approve the run. Recheck the task 1 values and investigate unrelated inventory activity

  • ProblemStatus stuck on Free

    Not approved — Actions➔Approve

  • ProblemOn-hand looks sufficient but the order will not fill

    Check Allocated — much of the on-hand may be committed elsewhere. See task 1, step 4

  • ProblemClicking RELEASE TO WAREHOUSING in Lines ready for does nothing

    That panel counts lines; it does not act. Use Actions➔Release

  • ProblemOrder absent from the release selection

    Upto Release Date is earlier than the order line's Release Date (planned delivery date minus outbound lead time)

  • ProblemNo warehousing order

    Release did not run. Check Activities 1 at task 3, step 8 — if it reads Free, run it from Actions➔Release

  • ProblemActivity shows Automatic: No

    That activity never fires on approval in this configuration. Run it by hand

  • ProblemNothing under Outbound Open

    No warehousing order — return to task 3

  • ProblemYour order is not in the Outbound grid

    Wrong Order filter, or the release never ran — see task 3, step 8

  • ProblemCannot find Outbound Order Lines

    There is no such menu entry. Filter the Manager Dashboard's order grid and drill in

  • ProblemAdvice greyed out on the Actions menu

    You are on the session toolbar. The advice actions live on the Outbound Lines toolbar — see task 4, step 5

  • ProblemGenerate Advice greyed out

    Advice already exists. Use Undo Advice to start over

  • ProblemRelease Advice greyed out

    No advice exists yet. Run Generate Advice first

  • ProblemAdvice already generated before you ran it

    Some configurations generate it automatically on release. Check Advised Quantity first

  • ProblemOrder will not advise

    Header Warehouse does not hold the stock. Recheck against task 1, step 4

  • ProblemNo shipment number after releasing advice

    Expected in the standard flow. Continue through Pick Run, then record Shipment from Shipment Lines at task 5, step 6. An early line appears only when projected-shipment behavior applies

  • ProblemNo Picking node under Warehousing

    There is none. Picking sits inside Outbound/Inspections

  • ProblemGoods still need picking after Release Advice

    Expected. Released and Picked are separate. Run task 5

  • ProblemRun empty on the Picking List

    Advice was never generated, so nothing was released. Return to task 4, step 5

  • ProblemShipment will not confirm

    The line was never picked. Check the Picked column on Outbound Lines, then run task 5

  • ProblemShipment will not confirm, handling units involved

    If Handling Unit Based Confirmation is set on a linked line, the handling units must be confirmed first

  • ProblemAn item is absent from the Item Order Plan

    It has no cluster row. Step task 1, step 5. Not an error state; nothing will tell you

  • ProblemLN refuses the item on the sales order

    No row for the order's sales office on the Sales Offices tab of Item tcibd0501m100. Add it, then close and reopen the order session

  • ProblemThe demand does not appear in the Item Order Plan

    The delivery date is beyond the Order Horizon date. Step task 2, step 5 — and the date is not today plus your days

  • ProblemThe run plans the pair but not a component

    The component has no planning data of its own. Step task 1, step 4 — MRP skips it silently

  • ProblemA component has plan data and still produces nothing

    It may be correctly absent — planning proposes supply only for what stock does not cover. Read its own Item Order Plan and on-hand

  • ProblemThe pegging tree is empty

    Pegging relations were not generated, or the demand is beyond the Pegging Horizon in Planning Parameters cprpd0100m000

  • ProblemThe transfer runs and nothing happens

    The orders were still Planned. Step task 4, step 3. There is no message for "nothing matched"

  • Problem"Buy-from BP cannot be determined for item …"

    No partner row on the item's Item - Business Partner tab. Steps task 4, step 1–task 4, step 2. The failed proposal survives, so fix it and rerun

  • ProblemPurchase Order Type is blank

    LN gives an error. This environment defaults IPO

  • ProblemNo inbound order appears after the transfer

    Check the purchase order's Release to Warehousing tab; Purchase Order Line Status tdpur4534m000 names the activity a stuck line is waiting on

  • Problemwhinh0032 at the receipt

    Capture the LOG detail before clearing it, and read Errors Logged and Receipt Message Log whinh3530m000 afterwards

  • ProblemThe receipt confirms but on-hand does not move

    Whether All Lines Final and All Lines Complete were both set, and whether you re-read the warehouse from task 1, step 3

  • ProblemThe order will not release

    Printing Production Order Documents Mandatory in tisfc0100s000 may require Printed first

  • ProblemThe material line stays blocked

    Run Initiate Inventory Issue tisfc0207m000 manually; if still blocked, record what you saw

  • ProblemStatus reaches Production Completed and on-hand does not move

    That is the No path at task 6, step 5. Check Warehousing Orders whinh2100m000 for an open production receipt order

  • ProblemAdvice greyed out

    You are on the session toolbar. The advice actions live on the Outbound Lines toolbar — step task 7, step 3

  • ProblemThe order will not advise

    The header Warehouse does not hold the stock. Recheck against task 1, step 2

  • ProblemThe shipment will not confirm

    The line was never picked, or the shipment was never frozen. Steps task 7, step 4 and task 7, step 5

  • TaskChange or cancel an order lineChange or cancel a sales order line after it is entered.
  • TaskRush an orderGive a sales order, or one line of it, the highest priority through the warehouse.
  • TaskDirect deliveryHave the supplier deliver straight to the customer, so that Warehousing is not involved.
  • TaskCross-dockingFill a sales order that has no stock by taking inbound goods straight from receipt to the staging location.
  • TaskBlocked releaseStop a sales order line from releasing.
  • TaskSales returnsTake goods back from a customer.

  • TaskWarehouse transferMove stock from one warehouse to another.
  • ScreenTransfer Order PlanningConverts a planned order into a real order in its owning module — production, purchase, warehouse, or cost-peg transfer.
  • ScreenPlanning ParametersCompany-wide planning settings, among them the CTP check for sales, the pegging horizon and how many plan revisions are kept.
  • ScreenItems - PlanningHolds the order horizon, planning horizon and time fence that decide whether and how far ahead an item is planned.
  • ScreenCheck HorizonsCalculates a plan item's cumulative order lead time, and checks and brings into line the order horizons of the items in a bill of material.
  • ScreenScenariosDefines the scenario a planning run executes in — the horizon, whether the plan rolls, and whether the run is a net change or a full regeneration.
  • ScreenGenerate Pegging RelationsRuns the generation of pegging relations, in full or as a net-change update.
  • ScreenItem Order PlanA time-phased view of one item's order planning: demand and forecast against scheduled receipts and planned supply.
  • ScreenOrder PeggingShows the pegging relations between orders as a tree, one branch for each order.
  • ScreenPlanned OrdersLists the planned orders MRP produced, for review and selection before they are transferred to execution.
  • ScreenConfirm Order PlanningConfirms a range of planned orders in one run, and can take only those inside their order lead time.
  • ScreenGenerate Order PlanningRuns the range-based order-planning process that turns demand into planned orders.
  • ScreenGenerate Order Planning (Item)Runs order planning for a single item.
  • ScreenPlanned OrderOne planned order in detail: its order lines, which can be changed here, and the demand each was generated for.
  • ScreenImplemented Software ComponentsRecords which LN concepts and modules are switched on for this company.
  • ScreenBuy-from Business PartnerThe details screen where one buy-from business partner is entered or maintained.
  • ScreenBuy-from Business PartnersLists buy-from business partners and their status, for viewing rather than editing.
  • ScreenCompaniesHolds each company's own settings, among them its calendar and its currency system.
  • ScreenConcept ActivationShows and maintains the activation status of one LN concept, chosen upstream.
  • ScreenItem DefaultsThe default data template applied when a new item is created.
  • ScreenItem Code SegmentationDefines the segments an item code is made of.
  • ScreenItemsMaintains global item data at the company level — the centrally controlled item record and its subentities.
  • ScreenItemSpecifies and maintains one item's global data across its subentities.
  • ScreenItem DefaultsThe detail form behind Item Defaults, holding the default item data for one item type and item group combination.
  • ScreenItems by SiteHolds the per-site row for an item under multisite, where site data can mirror or diverge from the global item.
  • ScreenItem Defaults by SiteThe site-level counterpart of Item Defaults, holding default item data for a site, item type and item group combination.
  • ScreenItem Control and Defaults by SiteDecides, per site, which per-module item records are generated for a new item.
  • ScreenItems - OrderingGoverns supply-planning boundaries, lot sizing and ordering intervals — how much LN plans and in how many orders.
  • ScreenItem - Ordering DefaultsHolds the default ordering data for an item type and item group combination.
  • ScreenItem - OrderingThe global item ordering record — lot-size limits, intervals and safety settings that the site and warehouse levels inherit from.
  • ScreenItem GroupsDefines the item group half of the key — together with item type — that the item defaults chain is keyed on.
  • ScreenGeneral ProjectsRecords a general project as a code; the plan itself lives in whichever package claims it.
  • ScreenDepartmentsDefines departments. A work center needs one first, and its calendar can be set here.
  • ScreenItems - Purchase DefaultsHolds the default purchasing data — buy-from partner, unit, currency, receipt tolerances — for a new purchased item.
  • ScreenItem Purchase Defaults by SiteThe default purchase data that items take at one site.
  • ScreenItem - PurchaseThe global purchase data for one item, holding what is needed to buy it at all.
  • ScreenItem - Sales DefaultsHolds the default sales data for an item type and item group combination.
  • ScreenGlobal Update of Item with DefaultsAssigns new default values to sales items in bulk.
  • ScreenItem - SalesOne item's sales data.
  • ScreenProcurement User ProfilesHolds each logon code's procurement defaults, among them the purchase office, site, warehouse and purchase order type its orders start from.
  • ScreenPurchase OrderEnters, maintains and processes one purchase order and its lines on a single screen.
  • ScreenPurchase Order LinesOne purchase order line in detail, including the warehouse it is received into.
  • ScreenPurchase ReceiptsThe receipts booked against a purchase order. Receipts for a direct delivery are entered here by hand.
  • ScreenPurchase Order - Lines to be ReleasedA purchase order's lines that are waiting to be released to warehousing.
  • ScreenPurchase Order Line StatusShows which activity a purchase order line is waiting on.
  • ScreenPurchase Order Intake WorkbenchA dashboard of purchase-order activity awaiting attention.
  • ScreenRelease Sales Orders to WarehousingReleases a range of sales order lines to Warehousing, turning them into warehousing orders.
  • ScreenRelease Sales Order Lines to WarehousingThe entry point for releasing a sales order line to Warehousing; the release itself runs from a menu action here.
  • ScreenSales Order Line StatusLists a sales order line's activities and the next order step that must be performed.
  • ScreenSales Order Intake WorkbenchA dashboard of sales-order activity awaiting attention.
  • ScreenJob Shop Bills of MaterialManages bill-of-material header data for multi-site BOMs used in job shop production.
  • ScreenJob Shop List of MaterialsSpecifies the materials and quantities required to manufacture a product — a BOM's material lines.
  • ScreenJob Shop Bill of MaterialThe single-BOM detail view behind Job Shop Bills of Material.
  • ScreenStandard Cost Calculation ParametersThe module-level switches that decide what a standard cost calculation is allowed to do.
  • ScreenItem - CostingMaintains an item's cost data, within whatever the cost calculation parameters permit.
  • ScreenCost Calculation CodesLists and maintains named cost-calculation recipes that other sessions reference by code.
  • ScreenItem Standard CostsDisplays an item's actual and historical standard cost structures by date — read-only history.
  • ScreenEstimated MaterialsThe materials a production order is expected to use and the warehouse each is allocated from. It locks once the estimated costs are frozen.
  • ScreenMaterial to Issue for Production OrdersShows and maintains the material quantities that must be issued from the warehouse to the production centre.
  • ScreenClose Production OrdersSettles the financial side of a production order once its goods are already in inventory.
  • ScreenCalculate Estimated End Item Unit CostsCalculates the estimated unit cost of an end item.
  • ScreenItem - Production DefaultsHolds the default production data for an item type and item group combination.
  • ScreenItem - Production Defaults by SiteThe site-level counterpart of Item - Production Defaults, including backflushing and material-issue defaults.
  • ScreenProduct Engineering ParametersParameters for product engineering, among them whether change notes are active.
  • ScreenJob Shop Master Data ParametersThe parameter set that controls how routings, operations and work centres behave in job shop production.
  • ScreenWork CentersLists work centres, used for cost estimating and planning — not a one-for-one model of the physical shop floor.
  • ScreenWork CenterOne work center in detail, used where the Job Shop by Site concept is inactive.
  • ScreenWork CenterOne work center in detail, used where the Job Shop by Site concept is active.
  • ScreenRouting OperationsMaintains operation data by item and routing — the individual steps a routing carries out in succession.
  • ScreenJob Shop RoutingsLists job shop routing operations.
  • ScreenReference OperationsA read-only view of reusable operation templates — work centre, machine type, and standard times — that routings point to instead of retyping.
  • ScreenJob Shop RoutingManages routings by revision and site, displaying the data listed in Job Shop Routings.
  • ScreenProduction Order ParametersThe parameter set governing Job Shop Control — where material is issued from, printing requirements, and shortage checks at release.
  • ScreenProduction OrderViews and maintains one production order, covering both its materials and its operations.
  • ScreenProduction Order DistributionHow a production order's quantity is distributed, which can give more than one production warehouse order.
  • ScreenProduction PlanningShows a production order's operations, where an operation's dates, its next operation and task, and its scrap or yield are changed, and count points are marked.
  • ScreenReport Orders CompletedAn order-level view of production orders that must be, or have been, reported complete.
  • ScreenReport Operations CompletedReports quantities completed or rejected for successive operations on a production order.
  • ScreenRelease Production OrdersReleases production orders to the job shop, so material can be issued and hours accounted.
  • ScreenInitiate Inventory IssueIssues material from inventory to a production order, activating the corresponding warehouse order line.
  • ScreenProduction OrdersAn overview of production orders — identity, item, dates, status, warehouse and key quantities.
  • ScreenInventory Handling ParametersCompany-wide picking and shipping parameters, held as a dated history with one current set.
  • ScreenWarehousing Order TypesHolds the settings a warehousing order type gives its orders, among them its inventory transaction type and how its shipments and loads are built.
  • ScreenDefault Order Types by OriginLinks a warehousing order type to an order origin, so orders generated from that origin default to that type and its procedure.
  • ScreenWarehousing OrdersLists warehousing orders — the starting point for almost every warehousing procedure.
  • ScreenWarehousing OrderThe order that initiates and controls one inventory transaction in Warehousing, generated automatically or entered by hand.
  • ScreenActivities by Warehousing OrderSets which warehousing procedure activities apply to one order — the only place that can be changed for an individual order.
  • ScreenOutbound Order LinesReleases outbound advice for individual order lines.
  • ScreenOutbound Line Status OverviewShows, for one outbound order line, which procedure activities will run and the quantity progression they produce.
  • ScreenWarehouse Manager DashboardManagement overviews of inbound and outbound warehousing orders.
  • ScreenWarehouse Inspections OverviewWhere inbound and outbound inspections are viewed and maintained — the step that can hold a receipt.
  • ScreenGenerate Inbound AdviceThe activity that generates inbound advice for received goods. It is not available in a warehouse without locations.
  • ScreenWarehouse ReceiptCreates and confirms receipts — where inbound goods become inventory.
  • ScreenReceipt Message LogLogs the error and information messages raised by actions on a receipt line, kept readable after the dialog is dismissed.
  • ScreenShipmentsViews, maintains and confirms shipments.
  • ScreenShipment LinesThe only place a shipped quantity can be changed, before the shipment line is confirmed.
  • ScreenPicking ListConfirms an advised quantity as picked, where picking is an activity in the warehousing procedure.
  • ScreenShipmentViews and maintains shipments — where a shipment is frozen and confirmed and inventory finally leaves.
  • ScreenApprove Adjustment Order VariancesApproves adjustment-order lines that require approval — the second stage, not the booking.
  • ScreenWarehousesLists the warehouses defined for the current logistics company.
  • ScreenWarehouse - Item InventoryOne row per warehouse holding or expecting an item — where a warehouse to ship from is chosen.
  • ScreenItem - Warehousing DefaultsHolds the default warehousing data — lot, serial, ownership and cross-docking behaviour — for an item type and item group combination.
  • ScreenInventory 360The starting point for any question about where an item's stock is and what state it is in.
  • ScreenItem - WarehousingThe warehousing detail behind one item — location control, inventory-variance handling, and supply settings.
  • IdeaAvailable to promiseThe stock LN will still promise to a new order, worked out over time, and the second check on components and capacity that follows when that stock falls short.
  • IdeaBackorderThe part of a sales order line that the final delivery did not ship, which waits to be confirmed and then becomes a new line to deliver.
  • IdeaBusiness partnerAny party you trade with, where customer and supplier are two roles on one partner and not two separate records.
  • IdeaContract deliverableA second way to raise demand on an item, beside a sales order, which planning ignores until it is switched on and whose supply stays tied to its project.
  • IdeaOrder planningLN's name for what most people call MRP. It lives in the package called Enterprise Planning, beside master planning, which is LN's name for MPS.
  • IdeaOrder typeA code on an order that carries the procedure the order will follow, so changing it changes how the same order behaves.
  • IdeaPlanned orderPlanning's proposal to buy or make something, which becomes a real order only when it is transferred and can be thrown away until then.
  • IdeaReleaseLN's verb for handing an order from one module to the next. It changes a status and unblocks the next step, and it moves no goods.
  • IdeaScenarioOne complete planning answer. Every planning screen is scoped by one, and only the actual scenario is real.
  • IdeaSessionInfor's word for a screen. Each has a code, shown in the status bar, that names it exactly.
  • IdeaSite and warehouseFour things often heard as one: a warehouse is where goods are, a site where a business is, an enterprise unit who accounts for it, and a planning cluster what plans it.
  • IdeaWarehousing orderThe order that controls every movement of goods in a warehouse. Most are generated by sales, purchase and production orders, and a transfer is entered by hand.
  • IdeaWarehousing procedureThe list of steps an order takes through the warehouse, each one run by LN or left to you, which is why advice, pick, freeze and confirm do not always apply.
  • IdeaWIPThe value a production order has taken in and not yet delivered. Issuing material or posting hours books it, and the first booking makes the order Active.

Task

Change or cancel an order line

Change or cancel a sales order line after it is entered.

  1. change or cancel the line on the sales order; once it is released, the warehouse decides whether that is still allowed
  2. if the change is allowed, the outbound line follows it, and its advice and picking list are deleted
  3. if cancelling is no longer allowed, finish the shipment with a shipped quantity of 0 and return the goods to stock with a transfer order
  4. Not documented for this release.

Task

Rush an order

Give a sales order, or one line of it, the highest priority through the warehouse.

  1. choose Rush Order on the sales order, or Rush Order Line on one line; the order's priority becomes 1
  2. release it to warehousing, where its outbound lines are advised and processed before any others
  3. Not documented for this release.
Search

Task

Direct delivery

Have the supplier deliver straight to the customer, so that Warehousing is not involved.

  1. set the line's delivery type to Direct Delivery, by hand or from the shortage menu that appears when stock is short
  2. generate the purchase order for the line, from a purchase order advice or directly
  3. record the supplier's receipt in Procurement and send the delivery back to the sales order
  4. Not documented for this release.
Search

Task

Cross-docking

Fill a sales order that has no stock by taking inbound goods straight from receipt to the staging location.

  1. set the line's delivery type to Cross-docking, by hand or from the shortage menu that appears when stock is short
  2. generate the purchase order for the line, from a purchase order advice or directly
  3. release the purchase order and the sales order to warehousing
  4. Not documented for this release.

Task

Blocked release

Stop a sales order line from releasing.

  1. read why it is blocked: an order over the credit limit, overdue invoices, a margin exceeded, a failed export or letter-of-credit check, or a reason someone set by hand
  2. release it in Blocked Sales Order (Lines) tdsls4520m000, a session in neither menu extract
  3. a user can release only the kinds of hold their profile allows, set in User Profiles tdsls0139m000, Sales➔Master Data➔General➔User Profiles
  4. Not documented for this release.
Search

Task

Sales returns

Take goods back from a customer.

  1. set up a return order type in Order Types tdsls0594m000, Sales➔Master Data➔Orders➔Order Types, as Return Inventory or Return Rejects, with a warehousing order type that receives
  2. create a sales order of that type, and give it the original document and a return reason
  3. copy the lines from the original document; they arrive with a negative quantity and amount
  4. approve the order and release it to warehousing, which receives the goods
  5. release it to invoicing, then process it
  6. Not documented for this release.
